subject: Agriculture
title: The Irish Potato Famine
description: A quick, practical guide to The Irish Potato Famine.

hook.text: In 1845, a water mold destroyed Ireland's potato crop. One million died and another million emigrated.

buildup.text: Ireland's poor depended almost entirely on one potato variety—the Irish Lumper. It was a genetic monoculture.

discovery.text: Phytophthora infestans—potato late blight—arrived from North America and spread across Europe in weeks.

twist.text: British policies worsened the disaster. Ireland exported food during the famine—grain left while people starved.

climax.text: The famine reshaped Ireland permanently—halving its population and fueling Irish immigration worldwide.

punchline.text: One crop, one disease, one nation transformed forever.

quiz.question: What organism caused the Irish Potato Famine?
options: Phytophthora infestans, a water mold causing late blight
